issues.detail: The Hebrew proper name נָחָשׁ (Nahash, the Ammonite king) is transliterated as '蛇' (snake) instead of being kept as a personal name. This changes the identity of the character from a named king to a common animal, which would mislead a Chinese reader.

The place name יָבֵשׁ גִּלְעָד (Jabesh-gilead) is rendered as '基列的約別士' (Jabesh of Gilead), but the Hebrew is a single compound place name 'Jabesh-gilead'; the rendering splits it awkwardly and the transliteration '約別士' is not standard, though the meaning is still recognizable. The main issue is the name swap of Nahash.
